chapter: Chicago, Lee Collins and the road
title: Joining as banjoist and willing to go anywhere
summary: When others refused to travel, Danny said he would go anywhere on bread and water.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: And that's why Lee kept me. He said, "You straightened Ernest Kelly out." When I joined... They needed a banjo player, so they sent... They knew that I could play a little bit. They was always lookin'... Because a lot of... When you said, "I'm going on the road," a lot of musicians said, "I ain't going. Where are they going? It's going to be a bazah(?)," which mean ain't nothin' gonna happen. "So you're goin' out there? They ain't gonna make enough money. You're wastin' your time. 'Cause it ain't payday out there in them little old towns." So they tried another banjo player.

Now, (?) me, I wanted to...I would go anywhere, whether I get paid or not. This is a trip for me. I ain't gonna sulk and I'm not a big eater. So I could get me a slice of bread and some water, and make it -- and I don't care where it's at. And I wasn't afraid to go anywhere, because I could run like hell, and I figured if I got into trouble, if I could get in the woods, they ain't never gonna catch me. See? So I was never worried about going nowhere.
